newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Dalmatinska sees 70 pct '97 pre-tax boost.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Dalmatinska sees 70 pct '97 pre-tax boost.

text.p: Dalmatinska Banka, one of Croatia's top 10 commercial banks, said on Friday it planned to boost 1997 pretax profit to 44 million kuna or 70 percent from the calendar year 1996.
"We enjoy a very favourable rating as a bank, especially abroad," official Mladen Fain told Reuters. "We hope results will even exceed our plans."
Dalmatinska is based in the coastal town of Zadar and has branches in the capital Zagreb and ports of Split and Rijeka.
According to its business plan faxed to Reuters, the bank expects total income to rise to 261 million kuna or 20 percent from the 217.6 million recorded last year.
It sees an increase of 22.8 percent to 2.2 billion kuna in its balance sheet in 1997.
Fain said the bank had been negotiating new loans with foreign banks which are helping Croatia's economic development.

The bank obtained a new 20 million German mark loan from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), he said. It had already used a previous 20 million mark loan to help small farmers.
"Negotations on a $9 million loan with the World Bank are drawing to a close," Fain said, adding the loan was intended to spur private enterprise.
Dalmatinska is also poised to get another loan from a syndicate of central European banks. Fain said it was likely to top 15 million marks raised by the bank last year.
The bank had 14.77 million kuna net profit in 1996, down from 15.25 million in 1995 although its pre-tax profit rose to 26 million kuna from 18.25 million.

Dalmatinska is expected to be one of the next companies to get a full listing on the Zagreb bourse. Its stock, now traded in a segment for semi-regulated firms, closed 10 kuna higher on Friday at 400 kuna. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
